newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE SHARE INDEX MAY HEAD LOWER AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE SHARE INDEX MAY HEAD LOWER AGAIN.

text.p: Singapore shares were expected to slip lower again on Wednesday, continuing a strong downward trend that has sent the island's blue chip benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) to four-year lows this week.
Dealers said recent figures showing Singapore's economy recovering after a year-long manufacturing slowdown were supportive but offered little promise of an immediate rally.
Chart analysts said the STII, which ended almost unchanged, down 0.40 of a point at 1,893.46 on Tuesday, was vulnerable to a fall towards 1,800.
Singapore shares have been under pressure from poor results expectations, currency woes and worries over the possible merger of some domestic and foreign share tranche listings.
"The real news that's going to get the money back into Singapore is good results numbers, but we're not going to see those in the coming crop of interims," one dealer said.
